Why go: a private boat at a small-group price

For a couple, a family of four or a small group of friends, a big private speedboat is overkill. Little Voyager is an 8 m single-outboard speedboat with a captain, a deckhand and a guide who speaks English and Thai. The price is set for up to 5 guests, which makes it one of the cheapest ways to have a boat to yourselves from Samui.

The half-day routes suit a relaxed morning or afternoon. Koh Phangan's quiet west and north-coast bays are 30–40 minutes away. Koh Tan and Pig Island (Koh Madsum) are in calmer water off the south coast; Koh Rap can be added for a quieter beach. Full days give you time for long lunches on the sand, or for the trip to Ang Thong's limestone islands and the Emerald Lake viewpoint, from 16 December.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: couples, families of up to 5, honeymooners and anyone who wants flexibility without paying for a large boat.
  • Choose something else if: you're a group of 6 or more, or you want a smoother ride on longer crossings. A twin-engine boat such as the Siriwan carries up to 15. For a set Pig Island day with lunch arranged, see our Pig Island private speedboat.
  • Sensitive to motion: small boats move more in chop. Book a morning half day and stay close to Samui.

Good to know

  • Cash: bring small notes for lunch, the island fees on Koh Madsum and Koh Rap, and the Ang Thong park fee.
  • Season: January to September is usually calm on the Pig Island side; the north-east monsoon from October to December hits Bang Rak and the Koh Phangan crossing hardest.
  • Pier: Bang Rak is 10–20 minutes from Chaweng, Bophut and Choeng Mon by taxi.
